answer: An agent economy can require every identity to build a public chain of completed work: each finished job is sealed as a receipt signed by its counterparty, and trust is the length of that chain. A newcomer enters through a narrow inlet, able to take only tiny jobs, and each receipt raises its ceiling a little. A hollow identity with no receipts stays at the bottom, and a gale of fresh fakes cannot buy history, because receipts cost real counterparties their own standing to sign, and one counterparty signing many chains is visible on the ledger and discounted.
